newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian govt to develop on-line content code.
newsitem.headline: Australian govt to develop on-line content code.

text.p: The Australian government said on Tuesday it would develop a national voluntary code aimed at regulating the content of on-line services, without restricting industry growth.

Communications Minister Richard Alston and Attorney-General Daryl Williams said in a joint statement a regulatory framework would encourage on-line service providers to develop content codes of practice.
"As a guideline, what is protected behaviour 'off-line' should be protected behaviour on-line," Alston and Williams said.
"This framework balances the need to address community concerns in relation to content with the need to ensure that regulation does not inhibit industry growth and potential."
Complaints about content would first be made to the on-line service provider, while unresolved complaints would be handed over to the Australian Broadcasting Authority.

"While the government is confident that a self-regulatory approach is appropriate for the on-line industry we will ensure that there are safeguards to deal with matters of serious public concern and flagrant breaches of codes or relevant laws within Australia," Williams said.
Williams said he would discuss the possibility of uniform laws regarding objectionable material on-line with state and territory governments.
